unit: Lesson 6 Good for the Earth, Good for Us

sentences.en: Every day, we produce lots of waste, and the Earth is getting sicker and sicker.
sentences.ko: 매일 우리는 많은 양의 쓰레기를 생산하고, 지구는 점점 더 병들고 있습니다.

sentences.en: Do you want to save the Earth?
sentences.ko: 지구를 구하고 싶나요?

sentences.en: Then, join the zero-waste challenge, and share your stories.
sentences.ko: 그렇다면 제로 웨이스트 챌린지에 동참하고 당신의 이야기를 공유해 주세요.

sentences.en: Olivia: My birthday was last Saturday, and my family and I ate out.
sentences.ko: Olivia: 내 생일은 지난주 토요일이었고, 나의 가족과 나는 외식을 했어.

sentences.en: There were lots of leftovers, but we brought them home.
sentences.ko: 남은 음식이 많았지만, 우리는 그것들을 집으로 가져왔어.

sentences.en: The next day, I made a nice lunch out of them.
sentences.ko: 그 다음 날 나는 그것들로 맛있는 점심을 만들었어.

sentences.en: FYI, you can find great cooking ideas for leftovers on the Internet.
sentences.ko: 참고로, 남은 음식을 활용하는 멋진 요리 아이디어는 인터넷에서 찾을 수 있어.

sentences.en: Domingo: My dog tore my bag.
sentences.ko: Domingo: 내 강아지가 내 가방을 찢어 버렸어.

sentences.en: I wanted to buy a new one, but I thought again.
sentences.ko: 나는 새것을 사고 싶었지만, 다시 생각해 봤어.

sentences.en: I learned that reusing is important for zero-waste living.
sentences.ko: 나는 재사용하는 것은 제로 웨이스트 생활에 중요하다고 배웠어.

sentences.en: So, I decided to fix it and reuse it.
sentences.ko: 그래서 나는 그것을 고쳐서 다시 사용하기로 결심했어.

sentences.en: I’m not very good at sewing, and I don’t think that the bag looks perfect.
sentences.ko: 나는 바느질을 잘하지 못해서, 가방이 완벽해 보인다고 생각하진 않아.

sentences.en: I guess it’s all right.
sentences.ko: 그래도 괜찮은 것 같아.

sentences.en: Emma: I often use food delivery services, but today I didn’t.
sentences.ko: Emma: 나는 음식 배달 서비스를 자주 이용하는데, 오늘은 이용하지 않았어.

sentences.en: Instead, I walked to my favorite restaurant with a reusable container and picked up the food.
sentences.ko: 대신에, 재사용 가능한 용기를 가지고 내가 가장 좋아하는 식당으로 걸어가서 음식을 가져왔어.

sentences.en: I heard that plastic never goes away completely.
sentences.ko: 나는 플라스틱은 절대로 완전히 없어지지 않는다고 들었어.

sentences.en: I didn’t use any single-use plastic today.
sentences.ko: 나는 오늘 어떠한 일회용 플라스틱도 사용하지 않았어.

sentences.en: I felt good!
sentences.ko: 기분이 좋았어!

sentences.en: Minsu: Yesterday, I took some plastic and glass bottles to a recycling machine near my house.
sentences.ko: 민수: 어제 나는 플라스틱 병과 유리병 몇 개를 집 근처에 있는 재활용 기계로 가져갔어.

sentences.en: I put them into the machine one by one, and I got some points in return.
sentences.ko: 나는 그것들을 하나씩 기계에 집어넣었고, 대가로 포인트를 얻었어.

sentences.en: What can I do with those points?
sentences.ko: 그 포인트로 뭘 할 수 있냐고?

sentences.en: Well, I can use them like money.
sentences.ko: 음, 나는 포인트를 돈처럼 사용할 수 있어.

sentences.en: Don’t you think that’s cool?
sentences.ko: 멋지다고 생각하지 않니?

prep.def: something that needs great mental or physical effort to be done successfully
prep.example: Climbing that mountain was a big **challenge** for me.
prep.example_ko: 그 산을 오르는 것은 나에게 큰 도전이었다.

prep.def: to make or grow something
prep.example: This farm **produces** fresh milk every day.
prep.example_ko: 이 농장은 매일 신선한 우유를 생산한다.

prep.def: things that people throw away because they do not need them
prep.example: Please put your **waste** in the right bin.

prep.def: to make something less or smaller
prep.example: We should **reduce** the time we spend on our phones.
prep.example_ko: 우리는 휴대폰에 쓰는 시간을 줄여야 한다.

prep.def: to have a meal in a restaurant, not at home
prep.example: We **eat out** on Friday nights.

prep.def: food remaining after a meal
prep.example: Mom put the **leftovers** in the fridge.

prep.def: to use one thing as the material to create another thing
prep.example: He **made a boat out of** old paper.

prep.def: a short way to say 'for your information'
prep.example: **FYI**, the library closes at six today.

prep.def: to use again or more than once
prep.example: You can **reuse** this paper bag many times.
prep.example_ko: 이 종이봉투는 여러 번 재사용할 수 있다.

prep.def: to pull paper, cloth, or another material into two pieces
prep.example: Be careful not to **tear** the page.

prep.def: to make something work well again
prep.example: My dad **fixed** my bike yesterday.
prep.example_ko: 아빠가 어제 내 자전거를 고쳐 주셨다.

prep.def: to use a needle and thread to make or repair clothes
prep.example: Grandma **sewed** a button on my coat.
prep.example_ko: 할머니가 내 코트에 단추를 달아 주셨다.

prep.def: designed to be used once and then disposed of or destroyed
prep.example: Try not to buy **single-use** cups.

prep.def: the act of taking goods, letters, etc. to people's houses or places of work
prep.example: The pizza **delivery** took thirty minutes.

prep.def: in place of something else
prep.example: It was raining, so we stayed home **instead**.
prep.example_ko: 비가 와서 우리는 대신 집에 있었다.

prep.def: able to be used again or more than once
prep.example: I always carry a **reusable** water bottle.
prep.example_ko: 나는 항상 재사용할 수 있는 물병을 가지고 다닌다.

prep.def: an object for holding things, such as a can, box, or bottle
prep.example: Keep the cookies in a glass **container**.

prep.def: to disappear or stop being there
prep.example: My headache finally **went away**.

prep.def: in every way; totally
prep.example: I **completely** forgot her birthday.

prep.def: to put old paper, glass, or other materials through a special process so that they can be used again
prep.example: We **recycle** cans and paper at school.

prep.def: a piece of equipment that you use to do a job
prep.example: This **machine** makes ice cream.

prep.def: to carry something with you to a place
prep.example: Please **take this book to** the teacher.

prep.def: to place one thing inside another thing
prep.example: **Put the eggs into** the basket.

prep.def: one person or thing following another in order
prep.example: The students came in **one by one**.

prep.def: as a response, exchange, or reward for something
prep.example: I helped him, and he bought me lunch **in return**.
prep.example_ko: 내가 그를 도왔고, 그는 보답으로 내게 점심을 사 주었다.

ws8.answer: Every day, we produce lots of waste, and the Earth is getting sicker and sicker.
Do you want to save the Earth?
Then, join the zero-waste challenge, and share your stories.
Olivia: My birthday was last Saturday, and my family and I ate out.
There were lots of leftovers, but we brought them home.
The next day, I made a nice lunch out of them.
FYI, you can find great cooking ideas for leftovers on the Internet.
Domingo: My dog tore my bag.
I wanted to buy a new one, but I thought again.
I learned that reusing is important for zero-waste living.
So, I decided to fix it and reuse it.
I’m not very good at sewing, and I don’t think that the bag looks perfect.
I guess it’s all right.
Emma: I often use food delivery services, but today I didn’t.
Instead, I walked to my favorite restaurant with a reusable container and picked up the food.
I heard that plastic never goes away completely.
I didn’t use any single-use plastic today.
I felt good!
Minsu: Yesterday, I took some plastic and glass bottles to a recycling machine near my house.
I put them into the machine one by one, and I got some points in return.
What can I do with those points?
Well, I can use them like money.
Don’t you think that’s cool?
